items_missed: No agenda statement or 'sound good?' confirmation — opened with 'let me just go ahead and get the details of the move' and never told the customer what the call would cover or how long it would take
Never asked 'How are you today?' or any rapport opener
No packing-needs question, no additional-stops question, no moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')
Zero pricing structure — delivered a flat '$888 for the move' with no hourly rate, no per-mover breakdown, and no list of what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, tools)
No 'no hidden fees' pitch and no 'pricing is super simple' framing
No No Worries Damage Coverage mention — and the customer explicitly flagged art and two large TVs as 'delicate for sure,' which was an open invitation for it
No Meet Your Mover mention, despite the move being days away — exactly when that email lands
No On-Time Guarantee — gave the 12:15–2:15 window with no guarantee language attached
Entire Clock section skipped: no on-site start, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments
Estimate delivered without saying how many movers or trucks are coming

No Save Your Ass prep speech at all — the customer volunteered 'I'm starting to move over there on Wednesday and just driving back and forth with all my stuff,' and the rep answered 'Okay. Alright.' instead of reinforcing the carload/consolidation tip that would have shortened the move
No confirmation-email handoff explained — no bolded detail list, no 'reply with any corrections'
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' and no hours/how-to-reach-us; 'if anything comes up please give us a call' was the whole close
Used the customer's name once and mispronounced it ('Hi, Michelle' for Mitchell); leaned on 'sir' for the rest of the call
top_strength: Genuinely strong logistics probing for a 5.8-minute call: he pinned down both unit numbers, the 17th-floor origin, elevator reservation, loading-area parking, and then did the math out loud on walk distance ('fifty feet and seventy feet, it's around a 120... let's add a little bit of time for that'), plus TV count and sizes and a box estimate. That is the raw material for an accurate quote.
coaching_note: Arden gathered good detail and then dropped a bare number on it — 'three and a half to four hours, budget an overall of $888' with no hourly rate, no movers/trucks, no clock rules, and no differentiators. Even on a callback to an already-booked customer, the estimate has to come with structure and the Save Your Ass prep speech. The clearest miss: Mitchell said he's hauling his own stuff back and forth starting Wednesday and that his TVs and art are delicate — two handed openings for the carload/consolidation tip and for No Worries Damage Coverage, and Arden answered both with 'Okay. Alright.' Practice one habit: after every estimate, say the rate structure, the 2.5-hour minimum with 15-minute increments, and the prep speech, then ask 'does that make sense?'
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and deferential ('sir' throughout, warm sign-off, customer ended with 'Awesome, thank you so much') but transactional and choppy — a run of eight 'sorry's over a talk-over, a mispronounced name, and no acknowledgment of the customer's stated worry about delicate items.
